text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller says she was not responsible for the closing down of private television channel Flash TV, which was targetted by armed attackers last week.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan does not take part in a toast to Ataturk, the secularist founder of Turkey, proposed by visiting Azerbaijan President Haydar Aliyev.
- A barman is shot death after being shown on a private pro-Islamic television channel with the word "Allah" tattoed on his shoulder.
- A businessmen's organisation says it theoretically favours abolishing the military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) but says the political situation makes this impossible.
- Senior deputies in the ruling Islamist Welfare Party say the secularist armed forces would not be satisfied even if an anti-Islamist proposal to extend state education were passed.
- Turk Telekom is failing to keep pace with the evolution of the Internet and is thereby obstructing its development.
- Turkey and Israel agree to hold joint military exercises and modernise M-60 type tanks.
- Trading volume on the Istanbul stock exchange keeps dropping in response to concern about political uncertainty.
- The cabinet of ministers has not met for three weeks to avoid discussing extension of state education to eight years as demanded by the NSC in a crackdown on Islamist activism.
- Private school pupils are more successful in passing university exams.
- Industrial production rose 11.1 percent in March from a year earlier.
